title: Chapter 844
paragraphs: Chapter 844
Episode 210. Memories of the Past - Murakan (3)
The reply from Zipfel was a declaration of acceptance of their surrender.
However, it wasn't a sincere response, but mockery.
"Hand over the body of the Lord? These sons of bitches...!"
Silderay trembled and yelled.

They were asked to deliver Temar's body to Zipfel, and all the knights and guardians should be executed in Zipfel's land. Then, the common people, who are no threat at all, will be spared to serve as slaves.
Those were the conditions presented by Zipfel.

"I knew this would happen, Diana. The crazy thing was saying we would surrender to them in the first place. Do they have any reason to keep us alive? Showing the will to surrender simply shows them that we have no other options left."
Diana couldn't stop Silderay anymore. She was also barely suppressing her boiling rage.
"Silderay, how much time do you have left?"
She was asking about how much longer he could withstand the ghostification.

"I don't know. It could collapse at any moment. At most, maybe a few months. And when I lose my mind, I won't even know I've lost it. Just like those who've gone before... Maybe I'm already insane, it's that confusing."
"I'm in the same situation. We have our task defined. Until we lose our minds, we'll do whatever it takes to protect the Storm Castle and the Garden of Swords."
Diana decided that was also a way to keep her promise with Solderet.

Accepting all of Zipfel's conditions was not even surrender. It was simply agreeing to be tormented without resistance. It was not about keeping a promise. It was neither a move to survive nor a choice for the future.
"Right, I was worried you might accept these terms. It's clear that you're not insane yet, neither are you."
"But I don't know what will happen after we refuse. All we can do is this. Unless a miracle happens, our family will be destroyed."
"We have to create a miracle. Just as the Lord has always done."
"You should continue to standby at the Storm Castle. There's a high possibility that the attack will begin immediately once we refuse."
"What if they don't attack and just focus on manipulating history?"
"We attack first. We have to fight and inflict some damage while we are still sane, before we become monsters. The one saving grace is that it seems like Elona Zipfel is currently unable to act."
If Elona had been in good condition, there would have been no reason for Zipfel, who had secured a certain victory, to stay idle.
Excluding Temar and Murakan, the only member of Runcandel who could 'fight' with Elona was Sarah alone.
However, Sarah's body and spirit were devastated due to the continuous battles and historical manipulations.

Even now, Sarah wouldn't be able to stand against Elona. Even in the days when she could stand against her, it only meant she could fight a fight, winning was absolutely impossible. Even if all the Grand Knights gathered, they couldn't defeat Elona.
Zipfel knew that fact very well.
Nevertheless, the fact that they are not sending Elona means there must be a problem with her.
The historical manipulation that is turning Temar and the Grand Knights into ghosts.
Elona was obviously at the core of it, and as Diana expected, she was exhausted.

"I will return to the Garden of Swords and inform the members of this fact. I will also look for someone who can suppress the rampage of the Lord in your place soon. You've weakened a lot, so you don't need to handle the Lord yourself."
"Understood, Diana."
Diana immediately returned to the Garden of Swords.
On her way back, she also prepared a response to send to Zipfel. I have no intention of accepting your dog-like conditions, let's fight until death.
"Kin, was there any news from the housekeeper while I was gone?"
"None. I don't know where he went... he should be safe."
"Hmm, I think Leret ran away?"
It was Lokia's voice. As soon as she showed up in the dark hallway, Diana frowned.
"Lokia, watch your mouth. It's not enough to casually call the housekeeper's name, but you even blabber about him running away?"
"Ah, you're so rigid again. Why run away? For Leret, running away could be the best way to keep his promise with Solderet? Unlike us, he's a race that can live for an almost eternal time."
"Even if the family has weakened, the law has not collapsed. Stop your loose talk, this is your last warning."
"Yes yes, you're scary. But I'm not wrong, am I? The housekeeper might have made that decision."
"Then that's the housekeeper's will, and it must be the right choice, so we don't need to figure it out. We just have to do our part."

"Well, the housekeeper is not the type to betray us. If he had thought of betraying us, there have already been too many better opportunities. How many sweet offers did Zipfel make to the housekeeper and the fairies? The housekeeper never even hesitated."
"Why did you nag knowing that?"
"Diana, do you think this world is fair?"
"What?"

"I mean, in this world, if you had to choose, we are the ones who are pursuing justice and liberation, but we can't help but be more tormented than Zipfel, who is indulging in all sorts of historical manipulation and wickedness to become the ruler of the world. Is that really fair?"

"Nobody forced us to fight Zipfel. The Lord did not, we did not. We just couldn't stand by and watch what they were doing, so we stood up to fight them. It's not something we've done in hopes of receiving anything in return, so it's bound to be painful."
"Diana, you're really lucky. Not just you, but the others too. Oh, I should exclude one or two...like Bale, who doesn't have such a great mindset."
"I hope you're not one of those one or two, Lokia."

"I'm not thinking of betraying or running away. Rather, if Zipfel had cleanly accepted our surrender this time, I would have had to run away. As you know, I've tortured so many Zipfel purebloods that they've accumulated a lot of resentment towards me. Even if Runcandel and Zipfel became one family, there would be no place for me."
"That's fortunate then."
Then Diana and Lokia planned how to start the final fight with Zipfel.
Of course, there was no chance of coming up with a great move to turn the tide. They just had to think about how to maintain a bit more dignity as they faced the end.
"Well, I guess I have to go meet Padler."
"...Padler?"
After Idal was destroyed, Padler became a revenger threatening Runcandel. He didn't attack the powerless Shissols or the knights, but all the remaining Ten Knights were his targets. Even Sarah.

Padler was in the middle of recognizing that he didn't destroy Idal alone with Temer. He thought that the clan had betrayed him first and that Temer and the Ten Knights had destroyed Idal together. He was also becoming a specter of historical manipulation.

"Yes. It's the last stand, and with Padler, we're bound to take a big hit before we even start fighting. Like Murakan sent his colleagues, we should do the same. If we're going to die, we'll meet somewhere, so I won't be as sad as Murakan. This is also for Padler."
"Phew."

"I'm going now. Solderet, if that damned god shows himself, let him know. What is he preparing for when a colleague has reached the point where he can't help but kill other colleagues? If he has the power to create a barrier for the Lord, he should rather protect the remaining people."
And so, Runcandel began its final resistance.

It was a struggle that started without any particular hope, and the days followed with results that were not out of expectation. Just because Elona couldn't step in, they could only achieve a very small victory, and there was no change in the overall tilt of the situation.
Murakan woke up once again while such a war was going on. Again, he woke up after a month.
Next to him was Diana, who was lying in the same bed.
"Diana... Why are you so injured?"
"I got hurt fighting with Zipfel. Fortunately, all the wounds are treatable."
"Ah... I see. My head is so foggy, I don't know what to say."
Murakan immediately fell asleep again, and when he woke up, no one was in sight. The silence quickly brought back Murakan's painful memories.
When Murakan clutched his head and screamed, servants passing by the corridor rushed into the room. To Murakan, they looked like comrades he had killed.
His broken spirit had no strength to accept reality.
However, after that day, Murakan remained awake for several days, even months, without falling into sleep.
All he did was sit in a chair and stare blankly into space, but that alone was a great comfort to the members of Runcandel.
From yesterday onwards, an unexpected hope for the war had emerged.
"Murakan, how are you feeling today?"
Silderay sat next to Murakan and spoke.
"You haven't completely forgotten how to speak, have you? I heard from the servants that you sometimes say something coherent. I haven't heard it myself because I've been busy fighting Zipfel."
"Uh."

"I learned something yesterday, the situation with Elona Zipfel is much worse than we expected. So if you come back, we'll have a chance to win. If, just if, Solderet can fix your heart, and you can regain your sanity... we might really be able to turn the tide."
Murakan stared blankly, not understanding Silderay's words. Silderay didn't show any disappointment and put his arm around Murakan's shoulder.

"If Elona doesn't take action, we can buy quite a bit of time. Recently, I and others have definitely felt our spectralization weaken. Those madmen, the biggest reason Zipfel could gain an upper hand from us was Elona. Now that the war is nearing its end, they're pushing Elona away out of fear."
"Ah."
"Anyway, I brought some of your favorite fruits today. The chefs will soon make them into pies, so eat and gain some strength."
"Silderay!"
Suddenly, Diana's voice was heard. It was urgent, but a bright voice. Sensing good news, Silderay met her gaze.
"Diana, what happened?"
"We got a message from the Storm Castle. The Lord... He has regained consciousness for a moment and left an order!"
